sources.title: Vocabolario romagnolo-italiano
sources.linguistic_area: Romagnol, Ravenna countryside (Bastia, San Pietro in Vincoli, Campiano etc.)
sources.license: All rights reserved (1960); digitised copy on Internet Archive
sources.reliability_notes: Large dictionary with proverbs and idioms, based on the Ravenna countryside, not Rimini. OCR text is noisy: voiced z is rendered § ? ^. Entries cited: patacca, spatachéss, cvajón, cui, mèrda, géval, vaca, piòc, bdòcc, zèmbal, azidént, anticòr, smadunèr, burdèl and many proverbs.
sources.relevant_sections: Headwords and phrase lists; many proverbs under months/saints
sources.author: Libero Ercolani

sources.title: Lingua romagnola (Wikipedia in italiano)
sources.linguistic_area: Romagnol, all of Romagna incl. Rimini, Forlì, Ravenna, Imola
sources.reliability_notes: Gives vowel system, subject clitics, negation, articles, plurals, paradigms (essere, avere, magnè, pagh-é, vut-êr) with city labels and bibliography (Masotti, Pelliciardi, Vitali).

sources.title: Romagnol dialect (Wikipedia, English)
sources.reliability_notes: Orthography follows Vitali 2008; vowel table with examples (bël/bèl, fêr, cã), four conjugations, obligatory subject pronouns, impersonal avèr.

sources.title: patacca (Wikizionario)
sources.reliability_notes: Standard Italian sense: silver coin, worthless object. No Romagnol sense. Used to separate the Italian sense from the Romagnol one.

sources.title: patacca (Wiktionary)
sources.reliability_notes: Italian senses: junk or fake, medal, stain, vulgar term for female genitalia. Etymology uncertain. Documents the vulgar sense.

sources.title: andêr (Wikizionario, romagnolo)
sources.reliability_notes: Romagnol verb 'andêr' (to go), citing Giovannini 2025 course; confirms spelling with circumflex.

sources.title: Romagnol proverbs (Wikiquote)
sources.reliability_notes: 14 proverbs with English equivalents; spelling inconsistent and one entry misfiled (German). Used with normalisation.

sources.title: Proverbi romagnoli in dialetto con traduzione in italiano
sources.reliability_notes: About 50 proverbs with Italian translation; unknown collector, spelling uneven. Used only for short, widely known sayings that are confirmed elsewhere or very common.

sources.title: Perché si dice patacca? / Chi pataca? (areasosta.com FAQ)
sources.reliability_notes: Popular FAQ: 'pataca' as harmless show-off; quotes a San Marino RTV description as 'forse la più famosa delle parole romagnole' meaning 'minchione, sciocco'. No etymology.
